studyMaterials.subject: Effective Communications
studyMaterials.title: Academic and Technical Communication
studyMaterials.summary: Similarities and difference of Academic and Technical Communication

blocks.text: Formal Communication is the structured exchange of information, following predefined channels, hierarchy, and professional standards. It includes emails, reports, memos, letters, and other documented formats, ensuring clarity, authority, and consistency in workplace communication.
Formal Communication can be divided into Academic and Technical Communication.

Academic communication is the formal exchange of ideas, information, and knowledge in educational and research settings. It includes essays, research papers, presentations, discussions, and academic reports.

It uses clear, organized, and formal language to present arguments, explain concepts, and support ideas with evidence. Its goal is to communicate information accurately and effectively to an academic audience.

Technical communication is the process of presenting specialized information clearly and accurately to a specific audience. It is commonly used in fields such as science, engineering, technology, and business.
It includes manuals, reports, instructions, proposals, and technical documents. Its main goal is to help readers understand information, solve problems, or perform tasks effectively.

questions.prompt: A university student presents the results of a research study on climate change to their professor and classmates.
questions.explanation: It presents research findings to an academic audience.

questions.prompt: A software developer writes documentation explaining how users can install and troubleshoot an application.
questions.explanation: It provides instructions to help users install and troubleshoot software.

questions.prompt: A technician prepares a report detailing the procedures and results of a computer system repair.
questions.explanation: It documents procedures and results related to repairing a computer system.

questions.prompt: A researcher writes a literature review analyzing previous studies on the effects of social media on academic performance.
An engineer creates a step-by-step guide explaining how to safely operate a newly designed machine.
questions.explanation: It analyzes and discusses previous research using academic sources.
